blocks.title: Photocraft in the activity panel
blocks.description: Layers, masks, type and real PSD files — the upstream Photocraft editor running inside Astravia, on your own machine, with the file you opened in the workspace.

showcase.user_prompt: Open assets/cover.png in the Photocraft panel and save it back.
showcase.assistant_reply: Photocraft is open on the right. Select cover.png in the Explorer, press File → Open inside the editor — it loads the selected file directly instead of asking again — then use File → Save to write it back to the same path.

items.title: The real editor, unmodified
items.description: The panel serves the official Photocraft web build byte for byte. Upstream's wasm and JavaScript are not patched; only two thin files of ours are added around them.

items.title: Open and save inside your project
items.description: Opening uses the file you selected in the Explorer, and saving writes back through Astravia — so the bytes land in your workspace instead of a downloads folder.

items.title: The same editor in a browser
items.description: A local hub serves the editor on a loopback address, so you can also open it in the built-in browser panel or in your system browser when you want a second window.

items.title: Install the plugin
items.description: Add it from the marketplace. Nothing else needs to be installed — the editor's files are 11 MB, fetched once on first open into the plugin's data directory, and reused offline after that.

items.title: Open the Photocraft tab
items.description: The first open shows a preparation screen while the editor is fetched; after that it starts from cache without touching the network.

items.title: Select an image in the Explorer, then open it in the editor
items.description: Inside Photocraft, File → Open takes the file you selected in Astravia instead of showing a system dialog.

items.title: Save back with File → Save
items.description: The working copy is written to the same path. Export… asks where to save instead.

items.title: Optional: open it in a browser
items.description: The bar above the editor has two buttons — built-in browser panel and system browser — that open the same local address.

blocks.content: In the browser entry points there is no workspace binding: opening a file there uses the browser's own picker and saving downloads through the browser, because those pages have no access to your project. Working on project files happens in the Astravia tab.

No reliable access to GitHub? The plugin never depends on one host. If the download cannot start, the preparation screen prints an absolute path: put photocraft-web-0.19.0.zip there, reload the tab, and it is used as is — the file is still checked against the pinned SHA-256. A cache from an earlier install, a self-hosted copy via PHOTOCRAFT_PAYLOAD_URL, and a proxy mirror in the source list cover the same case.

Photocraft has no way to tell the panel whether a document has unsaved edits. Reloading the tab or switching documents asks for confirmation only when a save happened earlier in that session, so keep an eye on the editor's own title bar before closing.
